adjudication_label: Selection of disorder modeling approach (CPA vs. supercell)
canonical_question: Why was the CPA approach with the Akai-KKR package selected over supercell-based DFT methods for handling the chemically disordered nature of the fcc phase?

question_variants.question: Why was the CPA approach with the Akai-KKR package selected over supercell-based DFT methods for handling the chemically disordered nature of the fcc phase?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The paper states that the CPA approach with the Akai-KKR package was used for electronic structure calculations, but does not explicitly explain why it was chosen over supercell-based DFT methods for the chemically disordered fcc phase.

answers.answer: The text mentions that electronic structure calculations were executed using the coherent potential approximation (CPA) approach via the Akai-KKR package. It does not provide a comparative justification or reasoning for selecting CPA over supercell-based DFT methods for handling chemical disorder.
answers.measurement_outcome: Calculations performed using CPA, no alternative method comparison
answers.boundary_limitation: No rationale for method selection provided
evidence_spans: We report the magnetic properties of the as-cast high-entropy alloy (HEA) FeCoNiTi, characterized by a dual phase comprising the face-centered cubic (fcc) and hexagonal C14 Laves phases.
The HEA manifests three distinct ferromagnetic orderings at 1084, 214, and 168 K.
The emergence of the 214 K transition is attributed to the influence of the C14 phase.

source_evidence_spans: Electronic structure calculations were also executed utilizing the coherent potential approximation (CPA) approach. To this end, the Akai-KKR program package, [24] grounded in the Korringa–Kohn–Rostoker (KKR) method with CPA, was deployed.
